title: Dedicated: expose tier->shape mapping + validate unsupported region/shape combos
author: Ethan Park
release_notes:
- Terraform: Dedicated modules now accept `dedicated_tier` and `hardware_shape` with cross-field validation and region availability guards.
- Adds outputs for resolved tier/shape metadata for downstream dashboards/automation.
description:
Context
Dedicated throughput tiers are being standardized (Standard/Performance/Premium) and Sales/Provisioning needs a single source of truth for which hardware shapes are valid per tier and which regions can actually provision them.

This PR updates the Redwood Dedicated Terraform modules to:
1) expose an explicit tier + shape mapping surface area (so customer/workspace configs are readable and consistent with the tier matrix), and
2) fail fast at plan-time when a user requests an unsupported region/shape combo (or a tier/shape pairing we don't offer).

Motivation
We have a recurring class of provisioning failures where a workspace applies cleanly but the control plane later rejects the request due to fleet constraints (e.g., Premium + H100 in regions without H100 supply). The goal here is to shift those failures into Terraform validation so they are caught before merge/apply.

What changed
- New variables
  - `dedicated_tier` (string; one of: standard | performance | premium)
  - `hardware_shape` (string; canonical shape id e.g. l4-1x, a100-8x, h100-8x)
  - `region` remains the module input, but is now validated against shape availability.
- Validation
  - Validates tier values against enum
  - Validates shape ids against catalog list
  - Validates (tier, shape) pairing (e.g., h100-8x is Premium-only)
  - Validates (region, shape) availability against a curated allowlist (initially matching current fleet constraints)
- Outputs
  - `resolved_dedicated_tier`, `resolved_hardware_shape`, `shape_gpu_type`, `shape_gpu_count` for downstream tooling (dashboards, policy checks).

Notes / follow-ups
- The region/shape allowlist is intentionally conservative and will be updated as fleet availability changes. This is meant to reflect "can be provisioned" not "might be available with best effort".
- Future work (out of scope): auto-select shape from tier + target throughput. That logic lives with control-plane policy and the tier baselines.

Testing
- `terraform fmt -check` (pass)
- `terraform validate` (pass)
- Added unit-style validation tests in `tests/` via `terraform test` to cover:
  - invalid tier
  - invalid shape
  - invalid tier/shape pairing
  - invalid region/shape pairing

Docs
- Updated module README examples to include `dedicated_tier` and `hardware_shape` and to show common error output.

Related
- ENG-2210 (shape catalog + tier mapping in control plane)
- Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions project (admission control + packaging alignment)

review_conversation: Irene Choi (review): Can we make sure the region/shape allowlist is clearly labeled as 'fleet availability' and not a product promise? Also please add us (Infra) as CODEOWNERS for the catalog files.
Ethan Park (author): Yep — updated comments + README language to state this is provisionability based on fleet constraints. Added CODEOWNERS entry for modules/dedicated/catalog/*.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): H100 8x should be disallowed in eu-west-1 for now; we only have pilot capacity in us-east-1 and us-west-2. Also, do we have a path for exceptions?

Ethan Park (author): Updated allowlist to restrict h100-8x to us-east-1/us-west-2. Exceptions should go through the existing infra provisioning process; Terraform will intentionally block unsupported combos to prevent silent drift.
Mina Haddad (review): The error messages are good. Can we include the list of allowed shapes for the tier in the error output? That helps Sales Engineering debug quickly.
Ethan Park (author): Added allowed shapes list to the tier/shape error message (kept it short, referencing canonical ids).
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Any risk this breaks existing workspaces? We have some legacy configs that only specify gpu_count and rely on defaults.

Ethan Park (author): Default behavior is preserved if existing callers don't set `dedicated_tier`/`hardware_shape` (we keep the old path behind optional vars). The new validations only trigger when the new inputs are provided. Added migration notes in README.
Irene Choi (final): LGTM once CI is green.
